NOT WWOX EVIDENCE; no compound was tested. The article was found in PMC and the PMC open-data bucket under CC BY-NC.

group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-10-27: 'Ge Wanzhong[Author]' = 39; with AND Drosophila = 27; with AND WWOX = 0. The last author's name is ambiguous in PubMed; the counts are an order of magnitude, not an identification.
group_assessment.weighting: OBSERVATION: the Drosophila genetics, the western blots and the behavioural assays are first-hand work of a laboratory with a Drosophila publication record (27 of 39 PubMed hits carry Drosophila), so the method class is within the group's competence. INTERPRETATION: the group has no WWOX publication (0), so any statement about WWOX in this reading is mine, not theirs; the causal sentences (ISR is detrimental, ATF4 is the effector) are the authors' reading of partial genetic rescues and are weighted as interpretation, not as observation.

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Genetic (RNAi) suppression of GCN2 in the neuronal dPARS2-knockdown fly largely suppresses the developmental delay; the claim is 'largely', and the pupariation curve in Fig 6H still lags the control.
entries.snippet: Depletion of GCN2 in dPARS2-deficient animals largely suppressed developmental delay (Fig. 6G, H and I).
entries.anchor: Results, 'Inhibition of the GCN2 branch of the ISR suppresses pathological changes caused by dPARS2 deficiency'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Genetic suppression of GCN2 reduces the seizure-like phenotype (bang sensitivity, recovery time) in the neuronal dPARS2-knockdown fly; text says 'largely reduced or suppressed'.
entries.snippet: the seizure phenotype was largely reduced or suppressed in dPARS2-deficient flies lacking GCN2, as revealed by the reduced number of flies showing bang sensitivity and decreased recovery time compared with dPARS2-deficient flies alone

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The authors attribute the developmental AND behavioural impairment to the GCN2 branch; this is the authors' causal reading of a partial genetic rescue.
entries.snippet: Thus, the impairment at both the developmental and behavior levels in dPARS2-deficient flies is caused by activation of the GCN2 branch of the ISR.

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Genetic knockdown of ATF4 in the neuronal dPARS2-knockdown fly 'largely' rescues developmental delay and seizure-like behaviour; the knockdown efficiency measure (qRT-PCR) is cited to Supplementary Fig S8.
entries.snippet: downregulation of ATF4 largely rescued the developmental delay and seizure induction defects caused by dPARS2 deficiency
entries.anchor: Results, 'ISR activation triggers developmental delay and seizure through ATF4' (Fig 7D-H)

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Kinase resolution in the fly head: phosphorylation of GCN2 rises, PERK phosphorylation does not, total GCN2 unchanged.
entries.snippet: Phosphorylation of GCN2, but not of PERK, was increased in the head of dPARS2-deficient flies (Fig. 6A and B).
entries.anchor: Results, 'The GCN2 branch of the ISR is activated in dPARS2 deficiency flies'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Phospho-eIF2 alpha is raised in the dPARS2-knockdown fly head and global protein synthesis (puromycin incorporation) is reduced.
entries.snippet: The ISR was indeed activated in dPARS2-deficient fly heads, as determined by the increased P-eIF2α levels in elav-Gal4 driven dPARS2 knockdown fly heads compared with the control (Fig. 5A and B).
entries.anchor: Results, 'Activation of the integrated stress response in dPARS2 deficiency'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The ISR target-gene list was annotated manually from a mouse study, not defined independently; it is the basis of the 'ISR target genes increased' statement.
entries.snippet: Moreover, we manually annotated potential Drosophila ISR target genes based on a previous study in mice and observed an increase in the expression of many ISR target genes in dPARS2 knockdown fly heads compared with the control (Fig. 5E) [27].
entries.anchor: Results, 'Activation of the integrated stress response in dPARS2 deficiency'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Ldh (and most glycolytic genes) rise at the TRANSCRIPT level in dPARS2-deficient heads, and Ldh PROTEIN rises by Western blot (abundance); no Ldh activity, lactate, pyruvate or flux is measured, and the Ldh rise is interpreted as ATF4 activity.
entries.snippet: Our RNA-seq results showed that expression of most glycolytic genes and Ldh were upregulated in dPARS2-deficient flies compared with the control, indicating activation of ATF4 in response to dPARS2 knockdown in our fly model (Fig. 7A). Upregulation of Ldh was also confirmed by Western blot analysis (Fig. 7B and C).
entries.anchor: Results, 'ISR activation triggers developmental delay and seizure through ATF4'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The ATF4-to-glycolysis/Ldh step is borrowed from a previous S2-cell study under ER stress; in this paper Ldh is not measured after ATF4 or GCN2 knockdown (no sentence of the Results reports it).
entries.snippet: Previous studies have shown that Drosophila ATF4 (also named as crc) was able to induce glycolytic enzymes and Lactate dehydrogenase (Ldh) upon ER stress in S2 cells [48].
entries.anchor: Results, 'ISR activation triggers developmental delay and seizure through ATF4'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The mitochondrial lesion: OXPHOS subunit PROTEIN abundance is reduced for complex I (MT-ND1, NDUFS1, NDUFS3), II (SDHB), III (UQCRFS1) and IV (MT-CO2) in neuronal dPARS2-knockdown heads; complex V ATP5A is not reduced.
entries.snippet: Western blot analysis revealed that the levels of mitochondrial DNA-encoded complex I subunit MT-ND1 and complex IV subunit MT-CO2 were reduced (Fig. 2B and C).
entries.anchor: Results, 'Impaired mitochondrial function in dPARS2 deficiency'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Complex I activity is read by in-gel activity staining (NADH/NBT), not by an NADH-oxidation or respiration (flux) assay; reduced in heads and larvae.
entries.snippet: A decrease in the activity of complexes I, II and IV was observed in dPARS2 knockdown fly heads as well as dPARS2 knockdown larvae (Fig. 4A and B).
entries.anchor: Results, 'Impaired mitochondrial function in dPARS2 deficiency'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Complex I in-gel activity assay method: native gel stained with NADH and nitrotetrazolium blue (an activity stain on a gel, not a respiration measurement).
entries.snippet: For Complex I, native gels were incubated in 1 mg/ml NADH, 2.5 mg/ml Nitrotetrazolium Blue Chloride (NBT), and 2 mM Tris-HCl (pH 7.4) for 45 min at room temperature.
entries.anchor: Methods, In-gel CI, CII, and CIV activity

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Mitochondrial lesion is not shown to be upstream-only: the authors hypothesise that ISR activity rather than the mitochondrial defect itself drives the disease; the mitochondrial readouts are NOT measured after GCN2 or ATF4 suppression in the Results.
entries.snippet: raises an interesting hypothesis that dysfunctional mitochondria in dPARS2 deficiency activate ISR, and that ISR activity, rather than mitochondria-autonomous defects, triggers the progressive disease development
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on adaptive versus detrimental ISR

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The authors state ISR activation is detrimental in this model on the basis of genetic inhibition of GCN2 alone (paired with ATF4).
entries.snippet: Our results indicate that ISR activation is detrimental in the dPARS2-deficient model, as we found that genetic inhibition of GCN2 suppresses developmental delay and seizures.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on adaptive versus detrimental ISR

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: How the mitochondrial tRNA defect reaches GCN2 is unknown; the discussion proposes uncharged tRNA export, ROS or a mitochondrial protease, and cites the OMA1-DELE1-HRI axis as an alternative relay in other cells.
entries.snippet: It remains unknown how defective mt-tRNAPro aminoacylation activates GCN2 in the cytosol.

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The mechanism between ISR and seizure is not determined; ATF4 is named only as a clue.
entries.snippet: we have yet to determine the exact mechanism by which ISR activation causes developmental delay and seizures
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on adaptive versus detrimental ISR

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Authors' own limit: the fly models are not complete phenocopies.
entries.snippet: they should not be interpreted as complete phenocopies of the disease

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The therapeutic statement is prospective: the fly models 'can be used to screen' agents; no compound was tested in this article.
entries.snippet: We believe that our Drosophila dPARS2 deficiency models can be used to more clearly elucidate the molecular pathogenic mechanisms of PARS2 deficiency and to effectively screen potential therapeutic agents for the treatment of PARS2 deficiency related disease.

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: RNAi lines used for the suppression arms (stock identifiers).
entries.snippet: UAS-GCN2RNAi (BDSC, 35355), UAS-ATF4RNAi (THFC, THU5856)

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Seizure assay age: Results give 5 to 7 days, Methods give about 4 to 6 days; sex of the flies in the bang-sensitivity assay is not stated in either place.
entries.snippet: Five to seven-day old elav-Gal4 driven dPARS2 knockdown and control flies were used for the examination of seizure susceptibility.
entries.anchor: Results, 'dPARS2 deficiency leads to developmental delay and seizure'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Seizure assay age in Methods (4 to 6 days), at odds with the Results (5 to 7 days); no sex is given.
entries.snippet: Flies about 4–6 days of age were collected in batches of 10 flies under brief CO2 anesthesia (1–2 min) and maintained at least 18 h at 25 °C prior to the assay.

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Bang-sensitivity protocol: a 5-second maximum-speed vortex of vials of 10 flies; readouts are fraction of flies bang-sensitive and righting time.
entries.snippet: Vials were stimulated with a vortex mixer (Kylin-Bell, vortex-2) at maximum speed for 5 s.

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: No sex is stated for any behavioural or developmental assay; sex is named only for the RNA-seq heads (5-day-old females) and in the genetics crosses (virgin female F1, male F2-F4).
entries.snippet: thirty snap-frozen fly heads from 5-day-old females were used

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Statistics for the seizure proportions: Fisher's exact test between control and experimental group (figure replicates are 3 vials of 10).
entries.snippet: To compare the percentage of flies that displayed seizure-like behavior between the control and the experimental group, we performed a Fisher's exact test.

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Titration (GAL4-dilution) control exists for the dPARS2 transgene rescue: an independent GFP transgene did not reduce the bang-sensitivity of the dPARS2 knockdown. No sentence of the Results reports an equivalent control for the GCN2 or ATF4 double-knockdown arms.
entries.snippet: Importantly, the presence of an independent GFP transgene did not reduce these defects in dPARS2 knockdown flies, ruling out the possibility that the rescue may be due to the titration of the GAL4 protein (Supplementary Fig. S4D and E).
entries.anchor: Results, 'dPARS2 deficiency leads to developmental delay and seizure'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Human cell finding: the homozygous PARS2 V95I HEK293T clone shows raised P-eIF2 alpha, lower puromycin incorporation, higher ATF4 protein and raised P-GCN2 with unchanged P-PERK (HEK293T is a non-neural kidney line; a single clone).
entries.snippet: Increased GCN2 phosphorylation was observed in PARS2 V95I cells, indicating robust activation of GCN2 (Fig. 8N and O). In contrast, PERK phosphorylation was not altered (Fig. 8P and Q).
entries.anchor: Results, 'PARS2 V95I mutation causes ISR activation in human cells'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: The human-cell clone is a single homozygous knock-in clone from a low-efficiency edit.
entries.snippet: Even the efficiency of the knock-in was low, we were able to obtain the single cell derived clone homozygous for the PARS2 V95I mutation (Supplementary Fig. S9).
entries.anchor: Results, 'PARS2 V95I mutation causes ISR activation in human cells'

entries.proposition: FLY PARS2 (MITOCHONDRIAL tRNA-SYNTHETASE) MODEL, NOT WWOX EVIDENCE: Complex I activity is reduced and complex II is not obviously altered in the human V95I cells (in-gel activity), unlike the fly.
entries.snippet: The PARS2 V95I variant in human cells causes no effect on the activity of complex II, which is different from our Drosophila models
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on the V95I variant

Western blot abundance, N = 3 to 5 per bar.
